solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Silence follows one interrupting dance piece (6)

indicatorNotes.follows: to follow is to come after, so SH is placed after I
indicatorNotes.interrupting: an interruption breaks into the middle of something, so I+SH breaks into BOP

annotation.surface: A hush falls as someone cuts into a dance number.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dance piece' reads as one item of choreography; 'piece' is a chessman on its own, and 'dance' is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the diagonal-moving chessman is one of the pieces on the board.

entries.clue: ITV user in broadcast unwelcome (9)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are thrown out of order

annotation.surface: A television viewer finds something unwanted on the airwaves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits a clue about ITV, a British television channel, so it passes as scene-setting rather than an instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what pushes in uninvited is unwelcome.

entries.clue: Steep skinned thighs on vessel leaving river delta (4-7)

indicatorNotes.skinned: skinning removes the outside, so THIGHS loses its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, HIGH sits on top of what follows
indicatorNotes.leaving: the river leaves the vessel, so R departs from PITCHER

blocks.note: THIGHS without its first and last letters
a pitcher is a jug; R for river comes out
Delta is D in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A grisly kitchen scene: thighs stripped of skin sit on a jug at a river mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steep' first suggests soaking, which suits the kitchen picture; it is the slope sense, as of a roof.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the roofing sense: a roof with a sharp angle of slope is both.

entries.clue: Quiet gun overheard (5)

indicatorNotes.overheard: something overheard is caught by ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a piece is slang for a gun

annotation.surface: A silenced weapon that someone catches the sound of anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quiet gun' suggests a silencer, but 'Quiet' is the definition and 'gun' is PIECE, gangster slang.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stillness and calm, as in the phrase 'a bit of peace and quiet'.

entries.clue: Section friend recalled after Charlie’s silly talk (8)

indicatorNotes.recalled: to recall is to call back, so PART and PAL are read backwards
indicatorNotes.after: the reversed pair comes after C

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Charlie is talking nonsense about some part of a friendship.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both words at once: PART plus PAL, read backwards, gives LAPTRAP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: empty, pretentious nonsense, originally a trick to win applause.

entries.clue: Master and student covering yard in pine (5)

indicatorNotes.covering: to cover for someone is to stand in for them, so L takes the place of Y

blocks.note: L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
to pine is to YEARN; the Y for yard is the letter swapped out

annotation.surface: A teacher and pupil set among the pine trees of a garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Master and student' reads as a pair of people; 'Master' is a verb, and the student covers for the yard in YEARN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to acquire a skill thoroughly.

entries.clue: Spoilt periodically with crust of tea bread (5)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter of SPOILT is taken
indicatorNotes.crust of: a crust is the outside, so only the first and last letters of TEA

annotation.surface: A spoilt child picks at the crusts at teatime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tea bread' reads as one thing, a teatime loaf; the definition is 'bread' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a flat, hollow Middle Eastern bread.

entries.clue: Muscles on tops of calves twisted internally (5)

indicatorNotes.tops of: in a down clue the top of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Calves Twisted Internally

annotation.surface: Calf muscles that have been wrenched inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twisted internally' reads as an injury, and both words are only letter sources; 'on' is RE in its 'concerning' sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the plural of rectus, the name of several straight muscles such as those of the abdomen.

entries.clue: Flower bent to one side once adult’s dropped dish (7)

indicatorNotes.dropped: in a down clue, dropping a letter moves it lower, so the A of LEANT slides to the bottom

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest

blocks.clueFragment: bent to one side once adult’s dropped
blocks.note: bent to one side = LEANT (tilted); its A for adult then moves down to the end

annotation.surface: A wilting flower, and a grown-up who lets a plate fall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' usually means deleted, but here the A is not lost, only moved lower in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal.

entries.clue: Mark tense opening foreign letter (6)

indicatorNotes.opening: to open something is to get inside it, so T goes into SIGMA

annotation.surface: A tense moment as someone opens a letter from abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening foreign letter' paints someone unsealing an envelope; 'letter' is a character of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a mark of disgrace, or a physical spot on the skin.

entries.clue: Calculated speed of light sitting inside new LA attic (8)

indicatorNotes.sitting inside: C sits inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.new: made new, so LA ATTIC is rearranged

blocks.note: c is the physicist's symbol for the speed of light

annotation.surface: Someone measures how fast the light moves in a fresh Los Angeles loft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Calculated' seems to belong with the physics of light, but it is the definition, in its sense of carefully planned.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a calculated move is planned for advantage.

entries.clue: Flexible workers with post delivering second vitamin dose? (15)

indicatorNotes.delivering: to deliver is to hand over and let go, so the S leaves STATION

blocks.note: men = workers, as in management and men
a post is a station, as a duty station; S for second goes

annotation.surface: Flexi-time postal staff handing out a second dose of vitamins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post' and 'delivering' paint the postal service; the post is a station, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: taking vitamins to top up a diet is one kind of adding extra.

entries.clue: Lift inside of Tate taken by most of team (7)

indicatorNotes.inside of: the inside of a word is its middle letters
indicatorNotes.taken by: AT is taken into ELEVE, held within it
indicatorNotes.most of: most, not all, so ELEVEN loses its last letter

blocks.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven; the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A gallery lift taken by most of the sports team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lift inside of Tate' reads as the elevator in the London gallery; 'Lift' is a verb and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to raise.

entries.clue: Invite contribution to debate MP timetabled (5)

indicatorNotes.contribution to: a contribution is a part of the whole, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A member of Parliament is invited to speak in a scheduled debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invite contribution' reads as a Speaker calling on an MP; 'Invite' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to invite trouble is to tempt it, to lure or entice.

entries.clue: Right about old pub stocking east European ham? (11)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so RT runs backwards
indicatorNotes.stocking: a shop stocks goods by holding them, so INN holds E

blocks.note: Rt = right, as in Rt Hon

annotation.surface: An old inn stocking Eastern European ham.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like the cured meat on the pub's shelves; the question mark signals the theatrical sense, an actor who overplays, here a tragic actress.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an actress in tragic roles may, question-mark style, be a hammy one.

entries.clue: Attack group with assistance back at the front (8)

indicatorNotes.back: sent back, so AID reads backwards
indicatorNotes.at the front: the reversed AID is placed before TRIBE

annotation.surface: A military unit attacks with support brought up from the rear to the front line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attack' reads as a verb in the battle picture; it is the noun, a verbal attack.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bitter verbal attack.

entries.clue: American orbiter devoid of colour (5)

blocks.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter

annotation.surface: A grey American spacecraft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American orbiter' reads as a NASA satellite; 'American' is the definition and the orbiter is a moon.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone from the state of Iowa is an American.

entries.clue: Granny possibly inspiring island air that’s foul (6)

indicatorNotes.inspiring: to inspire is to breathe in, so MA'S MA takes I inside

blocks.note: a grandmother may be your ma's ma

annotation.surface: Grandma breathing in the bad air of an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags that a granny is only one kind of MA'S MA: she could be your pa's ma instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a noxious vapour.

entries.clue: Sprightly runner crossing Italy behind car (9)

indicatorNotes.crossing: the river runs across I, holding it
indicatorNotes.behind: in a down clue, the river comes after the car

blocks.note: a river runs; the Ural flows through Russia
I is Italy's international vehicle code

annotation.surface: A nimble athlete crosses Italy on foot, trailing a car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like the sprightly athlete; it is a river, which runs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lively and quick, like the messenger god Mercury.

entries.clue: Sibling’s issue when improvised record’s cut (6)

indicatorNotes.improvised: made up on the spot, so WHEN's letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.cut: EP is cut into the rearranged letters

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: A brother's problem when an improvised recording is edited.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a problem; here it is offspring, so a sibling's issue is their child.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by relation: a brother's or sister's son.

entries.clue: Drink another drink before beginning to skin onions (7)

indicatorNotes.before: in a down clue, NOG and GIN come above S
indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: nog is a strong ale, or eggnog

annotation.surface: A drinks-and-cooking scene: a quick tipple before peeling onions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Onions' is British slang for heads, as in 'off his onion', and NOGGINS is slang for heads too.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for slang: both words mean heads.

entries.clue: Conservationists on area suffer small nosey animals (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, NT follows A as if resting on it

blocks.note: the National Trust, a British heritage charity
to bear is to suffer, endure
s = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Wildlife workers in an area put up with prying little creatures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nosey' suggests nosiness; it is literal, the long snout of the giant anteater. NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic houses and land in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: anteaters have long snouts for probing termite nests.

entries.clue: No sole cooked with diced Ugli fruit (6,9)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooking changes what goes in, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder; 'diced' is part of it

annotation.surface: A menu offering no fish, just chopped Ugli fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diced' looks like the anagram indicator but is fodder; 'cooked' does the work. An Ugli is a Jamaican citrus, so 'Ugli fruit' tempts as one phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a well-known variety of yellow apple.

entries.clue: Folded part of garment left under large mirror (5)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, L for left goes beneath the rest

blocks.note: l = large, as on clothing labels
to ape is to mirror, imitate

annotation.surface: Checking a jacket's fold in a big looking-glass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mirror' reads as a looking-glass; it is a verb, to copy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the turned-back front flap of a jacket.

entries.clue: Wader immersed in detergent on the counter (5)

indicatorNotes.immersed in: plunged inside, so the answer lies within DETERGENT
indicatorNotes.on the counter: counter means opposite, so the letters run the wrong way

annotation.surface: A bird dunked in washing-up liquid on the kitchen worktop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' reads as the worktop where the detergent stands; it means running counter, backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a white heron that wades in shallow water.

entries.clue: Cad supports conclusion of overland explorer (5)

indicatorNotes.supports: in a down clue, a support goes underneath, so RAKE sits below D
indicatorNotes.conclusion of: the conclusion is the end, so the last letter

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a cad

annotation.surface: A scoundrel backs the end of an explorer's overland trek.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overland explorer' reads as one phrase, but Drake sailed; 'overland' only donates its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sir Francis Drake, the Elizabethan sea explorer who sailed round the world.

entries.clue: Bony conductor wearing uniform in empty concerts (5)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the outer letters wear U, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.empty: emptied of its middle, CONCERTS leaves C and S

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A thin conductor in uniform at poorly attended concerts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bony conductor' paints a gaunt maestro; the conductor carries sound, a small bone of the middle ear.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the anvil-shaped bone passes sound from the eardrum inwards.

entries.clue: Westbound Air Force carries sovereign (8)

indicatorNotes.Westbound: in an across clue, heading west means running right to left

blocks.note: to force is to IMPEL, here written backwards so the container can be assembled

annotation.surface: A military aircraft flying west with a monarch on board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Air Force' looks like one unit, the RAF; it splits into two words, and the whole container is then reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: supreme, relating to an empire or emperor.

entries.clue: Unrehearsed half of dance performed (6)

indicatorNotes.half of: take half the letters, here the first three of CANCAN

blocks.note: the cancan is a dance; half of it is CAN

annotation.surface: Only half a dance number was performed, without rehearsal.
annotation.walkthrough: The dance must be one that halves neatly, and CANCAN, the high-kicking Parisian dance, does.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a candid photograph: taken informally, not posed.

entries.clue: Nude maybe nursing extremely painful headache (8)

indicatorNotes.nursing: to nurse is to hold close, so SITTER holds PL
indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: a nude model sits for an artist

annotation.surface: A life model nursing a terrible headache.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely painful' reads as describing the headache; it only gives the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: a splitting headache, one that feels as though it will split the head.

entries.clue: Turns back to outcrop circled by hawks (6)

indicatorNotes.back to: the back of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.circled by: hawks circle their prey, and here SELLS draws a ring round P, holding it inside

blocks.note: to hawk goods is to sell them

annotation.surface: Birds of prey circling over the back of a rocky outcrop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hawks' paints birds of prey circling; it is the verb, to peddle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as nouns: a spell at the wheel is a turn.
